text:
yvonne: spike of ~30 Pending GPU pods in ap-southeast1, autoscaler keeps adding nodes then removing them. billing alert fired.
pat: are these long-running?
yvonne: no, short inferencers (30s-2m) with a strict anti-colocate label (isolation=hard). scheduler logs: ```FailedScheduling: 0/42 nodes are available: 36 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity; 6 node(s) had taints the pod didn't tolerate```
eli: classic fragmentation. We either relax affinity to preferred, use MIG slices, or keep a tiny warm pool.
maria: MIG sounds good if performance holds. We have some node.k8s.io/gpu-mig=true nodes in apse1.
yvonne: short-term low-risk fix: mutate pods in namespace public-infer that have isolation=hard and annotation allow-relax=true -> add preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution weight 60. Also increase gpu pool scale-down delay to 10m.
pat: scope mutation narrowly to avoid breaking teams who need strict isolation. Use namespace + label + annotation check.
eli: longer-term: add scheduler scoring to prefer packing existing GPU nodes before triggering scale-up.
maria: I'll run a 100-pod MIG perf test in staging and post results.
ops-bot: NOTE: maintenance window 05:00-05:30 UTC. Avoid risky deploys during that time.
yvonne: action items: yvonne -> webhook prototype; pat -> autoscaler scale-down change; eli -> scheduler scoring PR; maria -> MIG perf run. Canary planned in ap-southeast1 after maintenance.
